content.caption: Success rate versus scaling factor k (1–5) for MaTTS, MaTTS without aggregation and MaTTS without memory on WebArena-Shopping, under (a) parallel and (b) sequential test-time scaling
content.description: Two-panel combined bar-and-line chart. It plots success rate on the WebArena-Shopping subset against the test-time scaling factor k. The x-axis ticks are 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, with no x-axis title. Panel (a) Parallel Scaling is on the left and panel (b) Sequential Scaling is on the right. A shared legend across the top defines three series: light-gray bars are MaTTS w/o memory; a dotted light-blue line with hollow diamond markers is MaTTS w/o aggregation; a solid dark-blue line with hollow circle markers is MaTTS. Both panels share a y-axis labelled 'Success Rate (SR)', shown on the left panel only. It runs from 36 to 56 in steps of 4 (36, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56) with light horizontal gridlines. The axis does not start at zero, so the gray bars rise from a 36 baseline and their height differences look exaggerated. Every mark carries a printed value: gray numbers above the bars, dark-blue numbers above the MaTTS circles and light-blue numbers below the w/o-aggregation diamonds. At k=1 the two lines start from one shared point labelled 49.7 in both panels. The k=5 MaTTS labels (55.1 and 54.5) sit to the right of the last circle. (a) Parallel: MaTTS rises monotonically 49.7 → 50.3 → 52.4 → 54.0 → 55.1. MaTTS w/o aggregation goes 49.7 → 49.7 → 51.3 → 52.9 → 52.4, peaking at k=4 and then dipping. The MaTTS w/o memory bars go 39.0 → 39.4 → 40.6 → 41.7 → 42.2, small steady gains. (b) Sequential: MaTTS goes 49.7 → 51.9 → 53.5 → 54.0 → 54.5, with large early gains and then flattening. MaTTS w/o aggregation goes 49.7 → 50.8 → 51.9 → 52.4 → 51.9, peaking at k=4 and then dipping. The MaTTS w/o memory bars go 39.0 → 37.4 → 38.5 → 40.1 → 40.6, dropping at k=2 and ending only 1.6 above k=1. Comparisons: both memory-based lines sit roughly 10–15 points above the no-memory bars at every k. Full MaTTS equals the w/o-aggregation line at k=1 and is above it for all larger k. The gap grows to 2.7 points in parallel (55.1 vs 52.4) and 2.6 points in sequential (54.5 vs 51.9) at k=5. Sequential MaTTS leads parallel at small k (51.9 vs 50.3 at k=2; 53.5 vs 52.4 at k=3). The two tie at 54.0 at k=4, and parallel overtakes at k=5 (55.1 vs 54.5). Without memory, parallel beats sequential at every k ≥ 2 (39.4 vs 37.4, 40.6 vs 38.5, 41.7 vs 40.1, 42.2 vs 40.6).
